Jim, saw Cofense launched AI-driven campaign detection on the Phishing Defense Platform and that your research clocked AI phishing at one attack every 19 seconds.

That threat backdrop creates more in-market security accounts than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Cofense off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Jim, quick follow-up for Cofense.

With a new AI detection capability live, demand usually outpaces what the team can work, and most groups don't know exactly how many meetings it takes to hit the new number. The gap shows up late, then the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Cofense needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Jim, last bit of proof for Cofense.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Cofense's reply rate likely compares to other security software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jim, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority for Cofense this quarter, no problem at all. Timing matters most right as you push a new AI capability to market, and I know that stretch is busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a security GTM motion? I'll tailor it to Cofense either way.
